page: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is a shared-core, budget-oriented virtual machine instance within the e2 family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs allocated from a 1/8 shared physical core, supporting hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 1.0 GB of system memory, providing a low memory-to-core density of 0.5 GB per vCPU. No local storage or dedicated GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark results place the e2-micro in the bottom 10% across all evaluated performance categories. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yield performance scores of 132.9 and 171.0, respectively. Memory bandwidth is highly constrained, with cached small-block reads reaching 9.73 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads drop to 0.1 GB/sec and writes to 1.33 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores reflect these hardware limitations, and static web serving throughput is limited to 0.17 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-micro represents an entry-level tier designed for minimal resource consumption. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and highly restricted memory capacity, which makes it unsuitable for sustained compute-heavy or memory-intensive tasks. This instance is best suited for lightweight, non-critical workloads such as basic microservices, small development or testing environments, simple cron jobs, or low-traffic static web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is an entry-level, shared-core virtual machine designed for budget-conscious, low-intensity workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz with 2 vCPUs mapped to a 1/8 shared physical core. The instance is configured with 1.0 GB of system memory, lacks local storage, and includes no dedicated GPU resources. Performance benchmarks place the e2-micro in the bottom 10% overall, with constrained CPU and memory bandwidth capabilities, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 171.0 and static web serving throughput of 0.17 GB/sec. This resource-constrained profile makes the e2-micro highly cost-efficient for lightweight utility tasks, small development environments, simple cron jobs, and low-traffic static web hosting, while remaining unsuitable for resource-intensive or production-critical applications.
